This guide describes the prospective software workflow for a new trial. The
supplied synthetic data provide a complete first-use example and can be
replaced directly with trial-specific cumulative counts.

## 1. Specify and lock the design

```{r}
library(SAboinETB)

design <- setup_design(
  basket_names = paste0("Basket ", 1:4),
  dose_levels = 1:5,
  target_tox = 0.30,
  efficacy_null = 0.30,
  efficacy_alt = 0.50,
  cohort_size = 3,
  max_sample = rep(24, 4)
)

get_boundaries(design)
```

Archive the design object and decision boundaries before enrolment. Changes to
the locked configuration should follow the trial's formal change-control
process.

The versioned implementation supplies and records the technical borrowing
limits, stopping cutoffs, reliability discounts, and utility scores together
with the trial-specific inputs.

## 2. Enter cumulative interim data

The required columns are `basket`, `dose`, `n`, `tox`, and `eff`. Counts are
cumulative at the analysis cutoff. Each basket-dose combination appears once.

```{r}
interim <- example_interim_data()
interim <- validate_interim_data(interim, design)
```

## 3. Run and review the interim analysis

```{r}
analysis <- update_trial(design, interim, current_dose = rep(3, 4))
recommend_dose(analysis)
```

Review the local sample size and events before the borrowing-adjusted posterior
summaries. The recommendation table reports incoming toxicity and efficacy BESS,
the action, the recommended dose, and the prespecified rule supporting that
action. A recommendation is decision support; protocol-defined medical and
safety oversight retains final authority.

The prospective engine never recommends an eliminated dose. Immediate
de-escalation selects the highest active lower dose. If frontier extension is
not available, utility is evaluated only among previously tried, active, and
locally toxicity-admissible doses; the basket closes when that set is empty.

The current dose and the historical exploration frontier are separate trial
state variables. At later reviews, supply the preceding analysis so that the
last recommendation and all irreversible eliminations are retained:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
analysis_next <- update_trial(
  design,
  next_cumulative_data,
  previous_analysis = analysis
)
```

## 4. Inspect borrowing

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
plot_borrowing(analysis, endpoint = "efficacy", type = "similarity")
```

Inspect endpoint-specific similarities and directional donor BESS. Unexpected
borrowing patterns should trigger data and programming checks before the
recommendation is released.

## 5. Archive the analysis record

Store the locked design, validated cumulative input, package version, analysis
timestamp, complete recommendation table, and any committee-approved override.
The separately hosted web application exposes the same workflow and calls the
package functions directly. Open it with `SAboinETB::run_app()` or visit
<https://01a03253-f738-56f5-30c7-6829683c4a56.share.connect.posit.cloud/>.
